entities.evidence: יַהְוֶה explicitly names Yahweh as the one who saw mankind’s wickedness. The source tag identifies this divine bearer as LORD@Gen.1.1.

name_review_base.evidence: יַהְוֶה names the God who saw mankind’s wickedness. The source tag LORD@Gen.1.1 identifies the same divine bearer as the previous Yahweh proposal.

review.translation: [And|0] [Yahweh|1] [saw|0] [that|2] [the wickedness of|4] [mankind|5] {was} [great|3] [on the earth|6], [and|7] {that} [every|7] [inclination of|8] [the thoughts of|9] [their hearts|10] {was} [only|11] [evil|12] [all|13] [day long|14].

analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה is the subject of וַיַּרְא. The כִּי clause states what he saw: human wickedness was great on the earth.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־
analysis.sense: see or perceive that something is so

analysis.evidence: In וַיַּרְא יַהְוֶה, “Yahweh saw,” the name identifies the subject of וַיַּרְא. The following כִּי clause states what he saw.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: After וַיַּרְא יַהְוֶה (“YHWH saw”), כִּי introduces what YHWH saw, namely that human wickedness was great on the earth.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected subordinating conjunction without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: that (what is seen, known or said)

analysis.evidence: In כִּי רַבָּה רָעַת הָאָדָם בָּאָרֶץ, רַבָּה agrees with the feminine singular רָעַת and precedes it as the predicate. The clause says that human wickedness was great on the earth. The description of every inclination as רַק רַע כָּל הַיּוֹם underscores its extent.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute adjective used predicatively, with no prefix or pronominal suffix.

analysis.evidence: רָעַת is the construct form of רָעָה. In רַבָּה רָעַת הָאָדָם, “human wickedness was great,” הָאָדָם identifies whose wickedness is in view. The description of human intentions as רַק רַע, “only evil,” confirms the moral sense.

In רָעַת הָאָדָם, “the wickedness of humankind,” הָאָדָם completes the construct phrase. The verse describes human wickedness throughout the earth, and the singular suffix in לִבּוֹ, “his heart,” agrees with the collective noun.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun used collectively.

analysis.evidence: בָּאָרֶץ locates the wickedness of humankind (רָעַת הָאָדָם) on the earth. The collective הָאָדָם gives the statement a scope extending across the inhabited world.
analysis.morphology: Preposition בְּ with the definite article, followed by a singular absolute noun in its pausal form אָרֶץ.

analysis.evidence: וְכָל modifies the singular יֵצֶר in יֵצֶר מַחְשְׁבֹת לִבּוֹ, so רַק רַע (‘only evil’) applies to every inclination of his heart’s thoughts.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to a masculine singular construct noun.

analysis.evidence: In כָל יֵצֶר מַחְשְׁבֹת לִבּוֹ, מַחְשְׁבֹת לִבּוֹ specifies whose thoughts are in view and what has an inclination: “every inclination of the thoughts of his heart.” The judgment רַק רַע, “only evil,” describes the moral bent of those thoughts.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: מַחְשְׁבֹת לִבּוֹ means “the thoughts of his heart.” The construct plural links the thoughts to לִבּוֹ, while רַק רַע describes every inclination (יֵצֶר) of those thoughts as “only evil.”
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine plural construct, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: מַחְשְׁבֹת לִבּוֹ means “the thoughts of his heart.” The suffix refers to הָאָדָם, and מַחְשְׁבֹת identifies the heart as the seat of human thought.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix ־וֹ.
analysis.sense: thought: what one says and plans within

analysis.evidence: רַק immediately precedes the predicate רַע, so רַק רַע means “only evil.” Every inclination of the thoughts of the heart is described as exclusively evil, and כָּל הַיּוֹם gives the duration, “all day.”
analysis.morphology: Restrictive particle, uninflected, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: רַע predicates evil of כָּל יֵצֶר מַחְשְׁבֹת לִבּוֹ, “every inclination of the thoughts of his heart,” and agrees with the masculine singular יֵצֶר. רַק gives the force “only evil,” and the preceding רָעַת הָאָדָם, “human wickedness,” establishes the moral sense.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute adjective used predicatively.
analysis.sense: evil, wicked (of persons, hearts, ways, deeds)

analysis.evidence: כָּל modifies the definite singular הַיּוֹם. Together they mean “all day” and describe how long רַק רַע (“only evil”) holds true.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state.

analysis.evidence: כָּל quantifies הַיּוֹם as a whole span of time. The phrase כָּל הַיּוֹם means “all day long” and describes how persistently every inclination of the heart was רַק רַע, “only evil.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute noun with the prefixed definite article הַ־.
